result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.contract_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Contract two nodes by merging v into u. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11827-L11938){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.contract_nodes( u, v, self_loops=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Contract nodes](/assets/graphs/op-contract-nodes.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two nodes merge into one. Node C is absorbed into node B, which keeps its label; C's incident edges are rerouted to B, and duplicate edges collapse." width="100%"} Creates a new graph where node `v` is removed and all its edges are redirected to node `u`. If there was an edge between `u` and `v`, it becomes a self-loop on `u` (unless `self_loops=False`). This operation does not modify the original graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [u]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to keep (node ID or label). All edges from `v` will be redirected here. [v]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to merge into `u` (node ID or label). This node will be removed. [self_loops]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), edges between `u` and `v` become self-loops on `u`. If `False`, such edges are removed. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with `v` contracted into `u`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If either node does not exist. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `u` and `v` are the same node. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Contraction is a fundamental graph-minor operation: the surviving node $u$ inherits every edge incident to $v$, and any $u$-$v$ edge becomes a self-loop on $u$ unless `self_loops=False` suppresses it. The traversal costs $O(E)$ time and produces a fresh graph, so the original is left intact. Node $u$ keeps its label and attributes, and edge weights carry through unchanged; on multigraphs, parallel edges arising from the merge may collapse depending on how the underlying edge set is stored. Contraction is what drives the aggregation phase of Louvain community detection and underpins the reduced graphs used in minor-based algorithms like planarity testing. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#d534fe38 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a path: A -- B -- C -- D g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) result = g.contract_nodes("A", "B") result.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: "B" is gone entirely -- its connections were redirected to "A" instead: ::: {#3eb74d5f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} result.has_node("B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: When the two merged nodes were already connected to each other, that edge becomes a self-loop on the surviving node -- unless `self_loops=False` removes it instead: ::: {#9277def7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) with_loop = g.contract_nodes("A", "B", self_loops=True) without_loop = g.contract_nodes("A", "B", self_loops=False) with_loop.count_all_loops(), without_loop.count_all_loops() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (1, 0) ``` ::: ::: This makes contraction a convenient way to simplify a graph by merging nodes that should be treated as one -- for example, collapsing two adjacent nodes of a path: ::: {#acb31a2b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_path_graph(5) # 1 -- 2 -- 3 -- 4 -- 5 simplified = g.contract_nodes(2, 3) simplified.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 4 ``` ::: :::
